config.title: Logical properties (margin-inline, etc.)

intro.title: Logical properties (margin-inline, etc.)
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage layout that adapts its spacing based on the text direction, such as left-to-right or right-to-left languages. You will learn the core concept of CSS logical properties, which replace physical directions (like left/right) with logical ones (like inline/block) to create more flexible and accessible designs. The main technologies involved are CSS properties like margin-inline, padding-block, and inline-size. By the end, you'll understand how to use these properties to style elements in a way that automatically adjusts for different writing modes and text flows.
intro.usecase: Logical properties like margin-inline and margin-block are essential for building responsive interfaces that adapt to different writing directions and languages. Developers use these properties when creating internationalized applications that support both left-to-right (English, Spanish) and right-to-left (Arabic, Hebrew) text layouts. For example, in multilingual dashboards or e-commerce product cards, logical properties ensure consistent spacing around text regardless of language direction. This approach eliminates the need for separate CSS rules for different text orientations, making code more maintainable and scalable across global products.

objectives: Apply logical margin properties to control spacing based on writing direction
Implement logical padding properties to create responsive internal spacing
Configure logical border properties for direction-aware element borders
Construct layouts using logical sizing properties that adapt to text flow
Manipulate logical positioning properties to align elements relative to text direction
Update existing CSS code by replacing physical properties with their logical equivalents
Integrate logical properties with CSS Grid and Flexbox for direction-aware layouts

steps.title: Style the container with basic layout properties
steps.instruction: In your CSS file, create a rule for the container div to make it a flex container with a horizontal layout.
steps.hint: Use the display property with flex value and flex-direction with row value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will become a flex container that arranges its children horizontally.
successCriteria: The CSS contains a rule for the container
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've included both display: flex and flex-direction: row.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container isn't styled as a flex container yet. Try adding display: flex and flex-direction: row.

steps.title: Introduce margin-inline-start property
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for the first child div to apply margin-inline-start: 20px.
steps.hint: Target the first child div inside your container and set margin-inline-start to 20px.
steps.seedCode:
/* Add your CSS rules here */

/* Target the first child div and add margin-inline-start: 20px */
steps.expectedOutcome: The first child div will have a 20px margin at the start of the inline direction (left in left-to-right writing mode).
successCriteria: The CSS includes a rule for the first child div with margin-inline-start: 20px.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're targeting the first child div and using the exact property margin-inline-start: 20px.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're writing valid CSS and applying margin-inline-start: 20px to the first child div.

steps.title: Introduce margin-inline-end property
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule that targets the second child div and applies margin-inline-end: 20px to create space at the end of the inline direction.
steps.hint: Use a selector like 'div:nth-child(2)' to target the second div, then add the margin-inline-end property with the value 20px.
steps.expectedOutcome: The second div will have 20px of space added to its right side in left-to-right writing mode.
successCriteria: The CSS contains a rule for the second child div with margin-inline-end: 20px.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're targeting the second div and using the correct property name: margin-inline-end.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule for margin-inline-end on the second div is missing or incorrect. Check your selector and property syntax.

steps.title: Introduce margin-inline shorthand property
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for the third child div to apply margin-inline: 30px.
steps.hint: Target the third div using a selector like 'div:nth-child(3)' and set margin-inline to 30px.
steps.expectedOutcome: The third div will have equal spacing of 30px at both its start and end in the inline direction.
successCriteria: The third child div has margin-inline: 30px applied.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're targeting the third child div and using the margin-inline property with a value of 30px.
steps.feedbackWrong: The third child div should have margin-inline: 30px. Check your selector and property syntax.

steps.title: Change container writing mode to vertical
steps.instruction: Add the writing-mode property to the .container rule and set its value to vertical-lr.
steps.hint: The writing-mode property controls the direction of text flow. Use vertical-lr for vertical layout from left to right.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .container rule now includes writing-mode: vertical-lr, which will switch the layout to vertical orientation.
successCriteria: The .container rule contains the writing-mode property with value vertical-lr.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the writing-mode property might be missing or have an incorrect value. Make sure to add writing-mode: vertical-lr to the .container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container's writing-mode property is not correctly set. Please add writing-mode: vertical-lr to the .container rule to switch to vertical layout.

steps.title: Observe margin-inline behavior in vertical writing mode
steps.instruction: Add a comment in your CSS to note how margin-inline-start now creates top margin and margin-inline-end creates bottom margin in the vertical writing mode.
steps.hint: You can add a comment using /* comment */ syntax. Place it near the .container rule to document your observation.
steps.analogousExample: /* In vertical writing mode, margin-inline-start becomes top margin */
steps.expectedOutcome: A comment is added to the CSS file documenting how logical properties adjust in vertical writing mode.
successCriteria: A CSS comment is present that mentions margin-inline-start and margin-inline-end behavior in vertical writing mode.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a comment, but make sure it specifically mentions how margin-inline-start and margin-inline-end behave in vertical writing mode.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try adding a CSS comment that notes how margin-inline-start and margin-inline-end adjust in vertical writing mode.

steps.title: Introduce padding-inline property
steps.instruction: Add a new CSS rule that targets all child divs inside the container and applies padding-inline: 15px to add padding in the inline direction.
steps.hint: Use the descendant selector .container div to target all div elements inside the container, then add the padding-inline property with the value 15px.
steps.expectedOutcome: All child divs inside the container will have 15px of padding applied to their inline direction, demonstrating the use of logical padding properties.
successCriteria: A CSS rule targeting .container div with padding-inline: 15px is added to the stylesheet.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're targeting all child divs inside the container and using the correct property value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule for padding-inline wasn't added correctly. Try using .container div as the selector and padding-inline: 15px as the declaration.

steps.title: Compare logical vs physical properties
steps.instruction: Add a comment at the end of your CSS file explaining how margin-inline adapts to writing mode while margin-left/margin-right do not.
steps.hint: Write a comment using /* */ syntax to explain the key difference between logical and physical margin properties.
steps.analogousExample: /* Logical properties adapt to writing direction, physical properties do not */
steps.expectedOutcome: A comment explaining the advantage of logical properties over physical properties appears at the end of the CSS file.
successCriteria: The comment explains that margin-inline adapts to writing mode while margin-left/margin-right do not.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a comment, but it doesn't fully explain the difference between logical and physical properties. Make sure your comment specifically mentions how margin-inline adapts to writing mode while margin-left/margin-right do not.
steps.feedbackWrong: The comment doesn't explain the comparison between logical and physical properties. Try adding a comment that specifically describes how margin-inline behaves differently from margin-left/margin-right when writing mode changes.
